Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Adult male patient with severe intermittent frontal headaches mostly during work, mild associated nausea, reduced appetite, unintentional 5-pound weight loss, bilateral hand tingling, palpitations, intermittent shortness of breath at rest, and loss of libido occurring since job change  
- Known hyperthyroidism on thyroxine replacement therapy, adherent to medication; symptoms suggest possible thyroid hormone imbalance (Hyperthyroidism/Thyrotoxicosis) with high likelihood as primary diagnosis due to classic symptom constellation including palpitations, heat intolerance, headaches, weight loss, and neurological symptoms  
- Secondary consideration of anxiety/stress-related syndrome contributing to symptoms given high stress level, symptom timing during work hours, and absence of prior similar symptoms; likelihood moderate but neurological symptoms less explained by anxiety alone  
- Peripheral neuropathy (possibly thyroid-related or nutritional deficiency) considered as cause for bilateral hand tingling, likelihood moderate; no leg symptoms or focal neurological deficits to confirm  
- Intracranial pathology and medication-related side effects (e.g., thyroxine over-replacement) considered less likely; no focal neurological signs or medication changes reported (conflict noted with medication side effect DDx but not supported by medication adherence)  
- Planned clinical examination will assess cardiorespiratory system, and blood tests including thyroid function tests will clarify thyroxine control status  

Management Plan  
- Patient advised to attend in-person clinic appointment for physical examination including heart and lung assessment  
- Order thyroid function tests to evaluate thyroxine adequacy and thyroid status  
- Consider additional blood tests such as FBC and iron studies to assess for anemia or nutritional deficiencies if clinically indicated  
- Monitor neurological symptoms closely; consider further neurological assessment if symptoms progress or new signs develop  
- Address psychological stress with appropriate support or referral if needed  
- No immediate medication changes; reassessment pending lab results and clinical evaluation

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)  
- Thyroid hormone imbalance (Hyperthyroidism/Thyrotoxicosis) – High likelihood; symptoms align with known hyperthyroidism and presentation including palpitations, heat intolerance, headaches, weight loss, and bilateral tingling  
- Anxiety/Stress-related syndrome – Moderate likelihood; supported by high stress level and symptom timing but less explanatory for neurological symptoms and weight loss  
- Peripheral neuropathy (Vitamin deficiency or thyroid-related neuropathy) – Moderate likelihood given new bilateral hand tingling and underlying thyroid disease; further evaluation needed  
- Intracranial pathology – Low likelihood; consistent with headaches and neurological symptoms but no focal neurological signs or progressive worsening reported  
- Medication side effects/Iatrogenic thyroid hormone overdose – Low likelihood; patient reports adherence and no medication changes; symptoms consistent but no supporting evidence of over-treatment
